source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.5.4 Rear of Vehicle or Trailer - Lenses and Reflectors

question: On a combination vehicle, which part must be inspected for rear lenses and reflectors?
choice_a: Only the rear of the trailer
choice_b: Both the tractor and trailer rears equally
choice_c: Only the tractor's rear
choice_d: Neither, since it was already covered under Lights Operations Check
explanation: On a combination vehicle, you need only inspect the rear of the trailer.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.5.4 Rear of Vehicle or Trailer - Lenses and Reflectors

question: What must be inspected about air and electric connectors on the power unit and trailer?
choice_a: Only that they are the same brand
choice_b: That they are seated and sealed, free of damage, and locked into place
choice_c: Only that they are painted a matching color
choice_d: Only that they are less than five years old
explanation: Inspect that air and electric connectors on the power unit and trailer are seated and sealed, free of damage and locked into place.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: What must air hoses and electrical lines be inspected for?
choice_a: Only proper length for the wheelbase
choice_b: Only correct voltage rating
choice_c: That they are not cut, cracked, chafed, spliced, taped, or worn, with the steel braid/electrical conductor not showing through, and to listen for air leaks
choice_d: Only that they use quick-disconnect fittings
explanation: Inspect that air hoses and electrical lines are not cut, cracked, chafed, spliced, taped, or worn (steel braid/electrical conductor must not show through); listen for air leaks on air brake systems.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: To receive credit for the air and electric lines/connectors check, what must the applicant inspect?
choice_a: Only the connections on the trailer
choice_b: Only the connections on the power unit
choice_c: Only the connections visible from the driver's seat
choice_d: The connections on both the power unit and the trailer
explanation: You must inspect the connections on both the power unit and trailer to receive credit.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: Why must electric lines be inspected, per the manual?
choice_a: Damaged lines may result in loss of ability to communicate maneuvers (no turn or brake lights) to other drivers, which is a serious hazard at night
choice_b: They regulate the trailer's suspension height
choice_c: They control the fifth wheel locking mechanism
choice_d: They are required for DOT registration stickers
explanation: Damaged electric lines may result in loss of the vehicle's ability to communicate its maneuvers to other drivers (no turn, or brake lights); not being seen by other traffic at night is a serious traffic hazard and can lead to a crash.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: What must be inspected regarding how the electrical and air lines are routed?
choice_a: That they run through a conduit at all times
choice_b: That they are not tangled, crimped, or pinched, or dragging against vehicle parts or the ground
choice_c: That they are exactly the same color
choice_d: That they are shorter than the trailer's wheelbase
explanation: Inspect that electrical lines and air lines (if equipped) are not tangled, crimped, or pinched, or dragging against vehicle parts or the ground.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Air and Electric Lines/Connectors

question: What must be inspected about the fifth wheel skid plate?
choice_a: Only that it is greased with a specific brand of lubricant
choice_b: Only that it has a manufacturer's date stamp
choice_c: That it is securely mounted to the vehicle by the fifth wheel platform, and inspected for cracks, breaks, or excessive wear
choice_d: Only that it is painted black
explanation: Inspect that the fifth wheel skid plate is securely mounted to the vehicle by the fifth wheel platform, and inspect for cracks, breaks or excessive wear.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Fifth Wheel Skid Plate

topic: Fifth Wheel Skid Plate - Why Inspect
question: Why must the fifth wheel skid plate be inspected, per the manual?
choice_a: To satisfy a bridge weight regulation
choice_b: To verify compliance with local noise ordinances
choice_c: To confirm the correct paint finish
choice_d: A faulty or damaged fifth wheel skid plate and improper connection can result in handling problems, rollover, or separation of tractor and trailer leading to a crash
explanation: A faulty or damaged fifth wheel skid plate and an improper connection between the tractor and the trailer can result in handling problems, rollover, or separation of the tractor and trailer leading to a crash.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Fifth Wheel Skid Plate

question: What additional item, if applicable, must be inspected about the fifth wheel skid plate?
choice_a: Proper lubrication
choice_b: Battery voltage
choice_c: Tire pressure
choice_d: Coolant level
explanation: Inspect for proper lubrication, if applicable.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Fifth Wheel Skid Plate

question: What must be inspected about the kingpin?
choice_a: Its exact diameter measured with calipers
choice_b: That it is in place and not bent, damaged, or worn
choice_c: Its manufacturing date
choice_d: That it is chrome-plated
explanation: Inspect that the kingpin is in place and not bent, damaged or worn.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Kingpin, Apron & Gap

question: What should be true regarding the space between the apron and the fifth wheel?
choice_a: There should be a small gap of about half an inch
choice_b: The gap should equal the kingpin diameter
choice_c: The trailer should be lying flat on the skid plate with no gap between the apron and fifth wheel
choice_d: A gap up to two inches is acceptable
explanation: Inspect that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate and there is no space between the apron and fifth wheel (no gap).
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Kingpin, Apron & Gap

question: Why must the kingpin be inspected, per the manual?
choice_a: To confirm it meets a paint specification
choice_b: To measure trailer axle spacing
choice_c: To verify insurance compliance
choice_d: Wear or damage to the kingpin can result in handling problems, rollover, or separation of tractor and trailer leading to a crash
explanation: Wear or damage to the kingpin can result in handling problems, rollover, or separation of the tractor and trailer leading to a crash.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Kingpin, Apron & Gap

question: What must be inspected about the pintle hook?
choice_a: That it is securely mounted to the vehicle frame, with no loose or missing parts, cracks, breaks, or excessive wear
choice_b: Only that it is a specific weight rating
choice_c: Only that it is painted safety orange
choice_d: Only that it swivels 360 degrees
explanation: Inspect that the pintle hook is securely mounted to the vehicle frame, inspect for loose or missing parts including mounting bolts, nuts, pins, brackets, and clamps, and inspect for cracks, breaks or excessive wear.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Pintle Hook

question: Into what part of the trailer does the pintle hook connection lock?
choice_a: The trailer's kingpin
choice_b: The trailer drawbar ring/eye
choice_c: The trailer's fifth wheel apron
choice_d: The trailer's landing gear
explanation: The pintle hook is described as a tow hitch or receiving coupling which the trailer drawbar ring/eye locks into.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Pintle Hook

question: What must be inspected about the trailer drawbar ring or eye?
choice_a: Only its diameter
choice_b: Only that it is chrome
choice_c: That it is not bent or twisted, is secured to the trailer tongue with no loose or missing bolts, broken welds, or cracks, and is not worn
choice_d: Only that it matches the tow hitch color
explanation: Inspect that the drawbar ring or eye is not bent or twisted, is secured to the trailer tongue with no loose or missing bolts, broken welds, or cracks, and is not worn.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Trailer Drawbar Ring & Tongue

question: For an extendable trailer tongue, what must additionally be inspected?
choice_a: That the hydraulic extension cylinder is rated for 5,000 psi
choice_b: That the tongue extends exactly six feet
choice_c: That it has a manufacturer's warranty tag
choice_d: That bolts, locking pins, and cotter pins are in place
explanation: If extendable, inspect that bolts, locking pins and cotter pins are in place.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Trailer Drawbar Ring & Tongue

question: What must be inspected about the tow hitch or other mechanism, including sway bar/control if equipped?
choice_a: That it is securely mounted to the vehicle frame
choice_b: That it is rated for at least 10,000 lbs
choice_c: That it has a backup camera
choice_d: That it uses a ball size of 2 inches only
explanation: Inspect that the tow hitch or other mechanism is securely mounted to the vehicle frame; inspect sway bar/control, if equipped.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Tow Hitch

question: With a tow hitch setup, what does the trailer coupler rest on?
choice_a: The kingpin
choice_b: The trailer ball
choice_c: The pintle eye
choice_d: The landing gear pad
explanation: The description for tow hitch identifies it as a tow or receiver hitch and trailer ball, which the trailer coupler rests on.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Tow Hitch

question: What must be inspected about the trailer coupler?
choice_a: Only its paint finish
choice_b: Only its serial number
choice_c: That it is not bent or twisted, secured to the tongue with no loose or missing bolts/broken welds/cracks, and not worn
choice_d: Only that it is greased weekly
explanation: Inspect that the trailer coupler is not bent or twisted, is secured to the trailer tongue with no loose or missing bolts, broken welds, or cracks, and is not worn.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Trailer Coupler & Tongue

topic: Trailer Coupler and Tongue - Why Inspect
question: Why must the trailer coupler and tongue be inspected, per the manual?
choice_a: To verify VIN matches registration
choice_b: To calculate trailer payload capacity
choice_c: To confirm paint color compliance
choice_d: Wear, damage, cracks, or improper welds may result in loss of the trailer, leading to a crash
explanation: Wear, damage, cracks or improper welds in the trailer coupler and trailer tongue may result in loss of the trailer, leading to a crash.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Trailer Coupler & Tongue

question: For fifth wheel coupling systems, what must be inspected by looking into the fifth wheel gap?
choice_a: That locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin, with no play between kingpin and locking jaws/lever
choice_b: That the release arm is painted red
choice_c: That the safety latch is removable
choice_d: That the kingpin is greased with synthetic lubricant only
explanation: Look into the fifth wheel gap and inspect that locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin, and inspect for play between kingpin and locking jaws/lever.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Locking and Safety Devices

question: What must be inspected about the release arm on a fifth wheel coupling?
choice_a: That it is removed prior to travel
choice_b: That it is in the engaged position with the safety latch or lock (if equipped) in place
choice_c: That it is spring-loaded to open automatically
choice_d: That it is painted a bright color for visibility
explanation: Inspect that the release arm is in the engaged position and the safety latch or lock (if equipped) is in place.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Locking and Safety Devices

question: For coupling systems other than fifth wheel, what must be true of safety cables or chains, and breakaway cables?
choice_a: Safety cables must be replaced every year regardless of condition
choice_b: Breakaway cables must be disconnected during inspection
choice_c: Safety cables/chains must be secure, crossed, and free of kinks and excessive slack, and breakaway cables must be engaged
choice_d: Safety chains are only required on pintle hook trailers
explanation: Inspect that safety cables or chains are secure, crossed, and free of kinks and excessive slack, if present; breakaway cables must be engaged.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Combination Vehicles Only - Locking and Safety Devices

question: What must be inspected about the landing gear?
choice_a: Only that it is painted yellow
choice_b: Only that it has a manufacturer's plate
choice_c: Only that it retracts within 10 seconds
choice_d: That it is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged
explanation: Inspect that the landing gear is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 Trailers Only - Landing Gear & Clearance

question: If the landing gear is power operated, what must additionally be inspected?
choice_a: For air or hydraulic leaks
choice_b: For proper paint color
choice_c: For a functioning warning buzzer
choice_d: For a backup manual crank
explanation: If power operated, inspect for air or hydraulic leaks.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 Trailers Only - Landing Gear & Clearance

question: Why is landing gear clearance during turns important, per the manual?
choice_a: It reduces tire wear during turns
choice_b: Landing gear must clear the back of the power unit while turning, and damage to its supports may result in the trailer tipping or falling when disconnected
choice_c: It affects fuel economy during cornering
choice_d: It is required for DOT weigh station clearance
explanation: Landing gear must be raised properly so it will not strike the ground during travel and must clear the back of the power unit while turning; damage to landing gear supports may result in the trailer tipping or falling over when disconnected.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 Trailers Only - Landing Gear & Clearance

question: Where must reflective tape be inspected on a trailer?
choice_a: Only on the front bumper
choice_b: Only on the roof
choice_c: On the sides and rear of the trailer
choice_d: Only on the landing gear
explanation: Inspect that reflector tape on the sides and rear of the trailer are present and affixed securely to the vehicle.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 Trailers Only - Reflective Tape

question: According to the manual's note, reflective tape is only required for which type of vehicle?
choice_a: Straight trucks
choice_b: Buses
choice_c: Tow hitch combinations
choice_d: Trailers
explanation: Reflective tape is only required for trailers; some jurisdictional laws may require reflective tape for school buses.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 Trailers Only - Reflective Tape

question: On the CDL Vehicle Inspection checklists, which items are marked with an asterisk indicating automatic failure if not performed correctly?
choice_a: The air or hydraulic brake check
choice_b: The horn check
choice_c: The reflective tape check
choice_d: The wiper/washer check
explanation: The checklists mark '*air or *hydraulic brake check' with an asterisk and the note 'Automatic failure if not performed correctly.'
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Class A/B/C Vehicle Inspection Checklists

question: What restriction applies to marking the checklist during the actual test?
choice_a: Markings must be made in red ink
choice_b: No additional markings or writing may be placed on the list
choice_c: Only the examiner may mark the checklist
choice_d: Markings must be initialed by both parties
explanation: Applicants may use the checklist for the test and check off items as completed, but no additional markings or writing may be placed on the list.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Class A/B/C Vehicle Inspection Checklists

topic: Class A vs Class B/C Checklist
question: Which section appears on the Class A checklist (Tractor Semi-Trailer or Truck & Trailer or Bus & Trailer) but not on the Class B or C Straight Truck checklist?
choice_a: Lights Operations Check
choice_b: Steering Axle
choice_c: Combination Vehicles Only
